issue.title: Remote content viewer cannot open production rows, and owners refuse to serve transcript/output paths
issue.description: Found while consolidating research.46 (MacBook as main SASE TUI over remote agents) and verified in code plus one live athena `done.json`. Two independent root causes, both precise: (a) the TUI looks for content handles on summary metadata that never carries them and never calls the federation `detail` op; (b) the owner gateway rejects the transcript (`~`-prefixed `response_path`) and runner output (`~/.sase/workflows/...`) because they resolve outside the artifact root. Crosses sase and sase-core (Rust boundary: the content-root policy belongs in sase-core; bump `sase-core-revision.txt`). See the consolidated report's §2.1 #2-#3 and §6.1.

task_type_fields.impact: Every remote agent's prompt/transcript/output is unviewable from a controller: the bounded content modal advertised in docs/remote_dispatch.md cannot open anything, so a FAILED remote row shows no reason and a controller cannot read what a remote agent said. Blocks any MacBook-as-viewer workflow and degrades athena's view of apollo today. Fix spans both repos: hydrate detail (or carry handles) for the selected row, route content reads to the owning host, expand `~` and allow-list the chat/workflow-output roots on the owner without weakening the artifact-root check for arbitrary paths, stop caching empty growing-EOF reads, decode UTF-8 incrementally, and add a contract test using real gateway summary/detail shapes instead of hand-built handles.
task_type_fields.repro:
Python side (sase `9fd8a081f4`):
1. Select any real remote fleet row and run the `view_remote_agent_content` action (or `e`, which reroutes to it on remote rows).
2. `_content_handle_for` (`src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_remote_content.py:55-67`) reads `fleet_content["handles"]` / `["content_handles"]`.
3. `fleet_content` is filled in `_fleet_agents_rows.py:343` from the summary row's `ContentMetadataWire` (`handle_count`, `total_byte_len`, `kinds`, `supports_*`; `deny_unknown_fields`, no handles). Real `content_handles` exist only on `ResolvedAgentDetailWire`, and no Python code calls `FederationFacade.detail()`. So `remote_content_available()` is false for every production row. Tests pass only because they inject `{"handles": [...]}` by hand.

Owner side (sase-core `6df3bed3`):
4. Even with handles, `canonical_content_path` (`crates/sase_gateway/src/fleet_reads/content.rs`) keeps a candidate only if it canonicalizes under the record's artifact dir. A 2026-10-09 athena `done.json` has `response_path: "~/.sase/chats/202610/..."` (literal `~`, treated as relative to the artifact root, so canonicalize fails) and `output_path: "/home/bryan/.sase/workflows/202610/..."` (outside the root). Only `commit_diffs/*.diff` survives, so the transcript and runner output are never servable.

Also (from research report cdx, not re-run here): `RemoteContentClient` sends `content_range_sync` without an owner selector and `_first_host_payload` consumes `hosts[0]`; an empty EOF read of a growing file is cached as a permanent chunk; chunks are UTF-8-decoded independently.

issue.creation_reason: The remote content modal documented as shipped never opens on real fleet rows and owners drop the two most useful files, so controllers cannot read any remote agent's transcript or output; nothing tracked it.
